title: Cranberry Sauce
description: Priya Krishna's stripped-down Bon Appétit sauce: a bag of cranberries, sugar, water, and orange zest, cooked until the berries burst and set on their own pectin. A shot of whatever's on the bar stands in for the orange liqueur.
source: Priya Krishna, Bon Appétit — her mom's version of a fresh cranberry sauce she first had at a friend's house, cut back on sugar and brightened with orange zest. Ran on BA's site in "The Easiest Cranberry Sauce Recipe Is Also the Best" and in the November Thanksgiving issue as "A Very Easy Cranberry Sauce"; later republished as a standalone recipe.

notes: Whole batch (about 2 cups) split into 8 quarter-cup portions. Assumes all-white sugar at 150 g per ¾ cup and 6 g of zest per tablespoon.
Optional booze, nutmeg, and cinnamon are excluded, along with salt. Swapping in brown sugar barely moves the numbers.

items.note: can swap some or all for light brown sugar

items.item: orange liqueur, white rum, or vodka

directions.title: Cook
directions.text: Everything into a medium saucepan over medium heat: 12 oz cranberries, ¾ cup sugar, 1 cup water, 1 tbsp orange zest, a pinch of salt, 1–2 tbsp booze (about half a shot), and the warm spice if you're using them. Stir often so it doesn't stick and scorch. Done when the berries burst and it goes jammy and coats a spoon, about 10 minutes.

directions.title: Cool
directions.text: Let it cool before serving. It sets up on the cranberries' own pectin as it cools — no thickener needed.

notes: Orange zest is critical. The rest is negotiable.
Keeps 5 days in an airtight container in the fridge, so make it ahead.

deviations.what: White rum or vodka instead of orange liqueur, or nothing
deviations.why: Uses whatever's on hand. The theory is that a shot pulls out more flavor the way vodka does in vodka sauce — unproven, but no harm in it.

deviations.what: Optional pinch of nutmeg and cinnamon
deviations.why: A little warmth without burying the sharp cranberry bite. Krishna skips warm spice entirely.
